leads.title: Civil Marriage Act (Federal, 2005)
leads.documents: Nationwide legalization of same-sex marriage, establishing marriage equality legal status applicable in Nunavut.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as passed by Parliament on July 20, 2005 after Supreme Court reference in December 2004; text notes by July 2005 same-sex marriages recognized everywhere except Alberta, PEI, Northwest Territories and Nunavut, then nationwide after Act

leads.title: Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms - Section 15(1), Section 1, Section 33
leads.documents: Constitutional equality framework, reasonable limits (Oakes Test), and notwithstanding clause that govern LGBTQ legal status and enforcement in all jurisdictions including Nunavut.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; quoted verbatim: '15(1) Every individual is equal before and under the law...' with discussion of ss.1 and 33 application to ss.2 and 7 to 15

leads.title: Egan v. Canada, [1995] Supreme Court of Canada
leads.documents: Landmark ruling that sexual orientation is protected under s.15 Charter equality clause as an analogous ground.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as 'landmark decision in 1995, Egan v Canada' and 'Egan v. Canada' holding sexual orientation included within bounds of section 15

leads.title: Vriend v Alberta, [1998] Supreme Court of Canada
leads.documents: Ruling that failure to include sexual orientation in human rights law violates s.15; basis for subsequent inclusion in all provinces/territories including Nunavut.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as '1998 decision in Vriend v Alberta' finding exclusion from provincial human rights law was violation of section 15 Charter rights

leads.title: Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1968-69 (Bill C-150)
leads.documents: Decriminalization of same-sex sexual activity in private between consenting adults, foundational criminal legal status applicable in Nunavut.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as brought into force upon royal assent on June 27, 1969, introduced in 1967 by then-Justice Minister Pierre Trudeau

leads.title: Criminal Code s.159 repeal via Bill C-32 / Bill C-75
leads.documents: Repeal of discriminatory anal intercourse offence and equalization of age of consent to 16 (18 with trust/authority/dependency), enforcement law applicable in Nunavut.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as Bill C-32 incorporated into Bill C-75 tabled late March 2018, royal assent June 21, 2019; prior court rulings in Ontario, Quebec, BC, Nova Scotia, Alberta declared s.159 unconstitutional

leads.title: Expungement of Historically Unjust Convictions Act
leads.documents: Federal remedial machinery allowing destruction/removal of judicial records for pre-1969 homosexual acts and s.159 convictions.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as granted royal assent June 21, 2018 (French: Loi sur la radiation de condamnations constituant des injustices historiques), RCMP/federal departments and provincial/municipal police notification, Parole Board distinction expungement vs pardon

leads.title: Canadian Human Rights Act and Nunavut / Provincial-Territorial Human Rights Acts
leads.documents: Anti-discrimination and anti-harassment machinery in employment, housing, public/private accommodations; as of 2017 all provinces, territories and federal government explicitly include sexual orientation and gender identity.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as 'As of 2017, all provinces, territories, and the federal government explicitly include sexual orientation and gender identity as prohibited grounds'; notes federal Act limited to federal government/federally regulated workplaces, territorial laws cover schools, rental housing, health care

leads.title: Nunavut same-sex adoption legalization (2011)
leads.documents: Nunavut-specific family-rights status: Nunavut became last province/territory to legalize adoption by same-sex couples.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited as 'Nunavut legalized adoption by same-sex couples in 2011, and thus became the last province or territory in Canada to do so' following BC (1996), Ontario (1999), others

leads.title: Prime Minister apology (Nov 28, 2017) and Canadian Association of Chiefs of Police apology (Dec 2020)
leads.documents: Official government and national law-enforcement acknowledgment of historic oppression of LGBTQ/2S communities, enforcement attitudes and reconciliation commitments relevant to visitor safety.
leads.detail: No URL visible in text; cited with full Trudeau quote 'We were wrong. We apologize...' and CACP quote on International Day of Human Rights apologizing for institutional bias, creating Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Committee
